MINUTES
  ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  September 11, 2017

An adjourned meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 7:05 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
CHAIRMAN YOO.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIRMAN YOO led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Chair Yoo, Schachter, Scott, Zigrang

  Commissioners Absent:  Medawar, Carman

  Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE ADJOURNED PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING OF JULY 10, 2017.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  None

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL RESOLUTIONS THAT ARE PRESENTED FOR THE
  CONSIDERATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON TONIGHT’S AGENDA AND
  ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER,

  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM 6-A.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 20-17; APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: DAPPLEGRAY NEIGHBORHOOD; The Planning Commission
  will be considering a request to allow metal standing-seam roofs to be allowed on homes
  in the Dapplegray Lane neighborhood and potentially on a city-wide bases. Historically,
  the City has allowed metal roofing on out buildings, such as barns, and as architectural
  accents for bay window roofs, copulas, small dormer windows, etc., but not for the entire
  roof of a home. Pending the outcome of the Planning Commission’s policy direction on
  this matter, the City Council will consider this request at a future date.

  Planning Director Wahba summarized the staff report and provided options on design
  criteria if approval is considered.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  discuss this item and provide staff with direction.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG asked if this will be city-wide. Planning Director Wahba
  stated that it will start in Dapplegray but, if approved, will be applied city-wide.

  1
Planning Commission Minutes
September 11, 2017
   In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Planning Director Wahba
  stated that this item should be considered under Neighborhood Compatibility, then policy
  direction to staff, and ultimately to City Council.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER inquired if the cities allowing metal roofs have minimum
  requirements for the type of quality of materials. COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that
  in his experience there are unique standards that must be met prior to getting approval to
  install metal roofs.

  A general discussion was held regarding the durability, installation, and cost of metal roofs.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about a list of neighborhoods that have mandated
  CC&R’s. Planning Director Wahba stated that there is such a list and it is currently being
  used when someone comes in to apply for roofing permits.

  COMMISSIONER SHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER YOO so ordered.

  Samantha Swanson, 12 Sorrel Lane, stated that currently she is remodeling her barn and
  is at the point where a roof is needed. She would like to order a metal standing-seam roof.
  Ms. Swanson stated that the barn is not visible from the street.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the CC&R’s may restrict his type of roof and
  the process to approve a change to the code requires some time. COMMISSIONER
  SCOTT added that the HOA has standing to enforce the roof type due to the standing
  CC&R’s.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG, Planning Director Wahba
  stated that there were approvals for metal roofs for barns in this neighborhood in the past
  with HOA approval.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Planning Director Wahba
  stated that this project was approved by planning with Presidential asphalt shingle roofing.

  Sean Swanson stated that there are at least 15 out building in the neighborhood with metal
  roofs. Planning Director Wahba stated that the new HOA Board has taken a stricter stance
  on metal roofs on out buildings where that was not an issue previously. COMMISSIONER
  ZIGRANG suggested that the property owners install a cap sheet roof while this issue is
  being resolved.

  In response to a question by Samantha Swanson, COMMISSIONER SCOTT discouraged
  the property owners from installing the metal roof without the appropriate approvals and
  permits.

  Kurt Swanson, 18 Palos Verdes Lane, stated that the CC&R’s are no longer valid and
  stated that the HOA have no legal standing and stated that the question is neighborhood
  compatibility and he believes that this is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Kirk Retz, 18 Dapplegray Lane, stated that the CC&R’s are recorded against the property.
  Mr. Retz stated that it does not fit in with the ranch style of the neighborhood. The goal,
  when the allowable roof types were determined, was to allow materials that closely
  resemble shake roofs. Metal standing seam roofs may be compatible in other
  neighborhoods.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there may be confusion with what is considered a
  barn, such as a small storage sheds or a barn that is not fully enclosed, such as a metal
  roof cover over a horse stall.

  In a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Mr. Retz stated that while he was on
  the Dapplegray HOA Board, there were no approvals for metal roofs.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Mr. Retz stated that the
  CC&R’s have been enforced by the HOA.

  2
Planning Commission Minutes
September 11, 2017
   Paul Schwartz, 13 Sorrel Lane, stated that no one corrected the prior owner of the
  Swanson home when it was painted blue. Another home was painted bright green and
  that home was corrected. Mr. Schwartz provided a brief background on the history of prior
  discussions regarding roofing in the CC&R’s.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he is not against standing seam roofs, however, it
  needs to be architecturally compatible with the building and the neighborhood. In addition,
  he recommended that a survey be done to determine how neighbors feel about allowing
  standing seam roofs.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER questioned how to restrict it to Dapplegray and
  suggested it be a city-wide survey and added that there should be strong guidelines put
  in place.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that Planning has a list of allowable roof types by street.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG suggested surveying the HOA’s.

  Planning Director Wahba suggested taking this item before the City Council prior to
  conducting the survey and stated that this could go on the agenda on the first meeting in
  October.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT MOVED, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER SHACHTER,

  TO REFER THIS ITEM TO THE CITY COUNCIL ON WHETHER OR NOT TO
  PROCEED WITH STANDING SEAM ROOFS.

  Ayes: CHAIR YOO, SCHACHTER, SCOTT, ZIGRANG
  Noes:
  Absent: MEDAWAR, CARMAN
  Abstain:

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 21-17; APPLICANT: VANCOUVER SIGN CO.;
  LOCATION: 608 SILVER SPUR RD.; A Precise Plan of Design to amend the Master Sign
  Program for 608 Silver Spur Road, to add one new exterior sign to the existing building.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a brief summary of the staff report and stated that staff
  recommends that this item be approved.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that Vista Sotheby’s sign is 2’x2’ and this proposal is
  20 1/4” and stated that it could go at least one size up. In comparison, the proposed sign
  looks too small. Planning Director Wahba agreed and stated that the applicant will be
  encouraged to increase the size of the sign.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER, Planning Director Wahba
  stated that the illumination of the sign is for visibility at night.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT MOVED, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER SHACHTER,

  TO APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 21-17 WITH DIRECTION FOR
  STAFF TO APPROVE THE SIGN IN THE 2’ TO 3’ HEIGHT RANGE.

  Ayes: CHAIR YOO, SCHACHTER, SCOTT, ZIGRANG
  Noes:
  Absent: MEDAWAR, CARMAN
  Abstain:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that this approval will have a 20-day appeal period.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 18-17; APPLICANT: ST. LUKE’S PRESBYTERIAN
  CHURCH.; LOCATION: 26825 ROLLING HILLS ROAD; A Conditional Use Permit is
  requested to allow the expansion of the existing parking lot. A Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination is requested for new construction of a parking lot adjacent to residentially-
  zoned property.

  3
Planning Commission Minutes
September 11, 2017
   Associate Planner Thom provided a summary of the staff report and stated that staff
  recommends that the Planning Commission open the public hearing, take public testimony,
  discuss the issue, close the public hearing, and adopt Resolutions No. PA-18-17.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the proposed parking move closer to the
  structures on the property and away from the homes. Planning Director Wahba suggested
  moving in the easterly direction.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER MOVED, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

  Sunny Kang, Pastor, St. Luke’s Presbyterian Church, stated that there is a need for more
  accessible parking for their aging congregation and people with small children in strollers.
  The primary parking on the north side requires that visitor navigate through 20 stairs to
  get the church building. There are only three handicapped parking spaces at this time.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about the location of the church entrance relative to
  the main parking and stated that the proposed parking is further away. Pastor Kang stated
  that the main entry to the church is on the south side and there are no stairs to the
  proposed parking.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT inquired about the buildings shown on the plans. Pastor Kang
  stated that they are buildings that have always been there.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that on the plans there is a reference to an area
  labeled “heavy vegetation”, but it is just dirt with bricks and concrete and asked if the
  church would be willing to plant trees in that area. Pastor Kang stated that in the southeast
  corner, 10 trees were planted, but there are plans to plant more. Pastor Kang added that
  they were in contact with Edison informing them of growing vegetation but were directed
  not to trim them since there are electrical lines. Eventually, one of the branches caught
  fire from the transformer and they were ordered to cut the vegetation and the church was
  cited. Pastor Kang stated that cutting the vegetation cost approximately $13K.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the proposed parking does not provide much
  additional parking. Pastor Kang stated that it will not solve the parking issue but it is what
  can be done at this time.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Ted Peet, Elder, St. Luke’s
  Presbyterian Church, stated that the location of parking area was chosen because it will
  meet the ADA requirement with regards to elevation. Planning Director Wahba stated that
  there are two additional sheds that are not shown on the plan and that may also be a
  reason for the location of the proposed parking lot.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Mr. Peet stated that there
  is a plan in place to install a small brick wall along the road way to control the water flowing
  onto the Montessori school playground.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there is an ADA compliant ramp from the parking
  lot to the church. Mr. Peet stated that the elevation change below is too great.

  CHAIRMAN YOO asked if the space is currently being used for parking. Mr. Peet stated
  that it is being used for parking for a couple of years.

  Michelle Goodwin, 3524 Lariat Lane, stated that there were more trees than Edison was
  responsible for and there was a serious fire hazard. A channel was created from the
  discharge pipe and is being diverted to the storm drain and eroded the trail. Ms. Goodwin
  stated that the whole facility should have been built with sufficient parking. There is
  excessive noise coming from the property. Ms. Goodwin stated that she along with other
  residents are opposed to this parking lot and it is not sufficient parking. Ms. Goodwin
  stated questions whether the parking lot is going to be used for other things and stated
  that the parking situation could be handled differently rather than disturbing the neighbors.

  In response to a question by CHAIRMAN YOO, Ms. Goodwin stated that there was a
  sports court installed with no permit and the City asked the church to remove it. There are

  4
Planning Commission Minutes
September 11, 2017
   children that are using remote control cars and stated that there are loud sudden noises
  and could also be a cause for concern for horse riders.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that Ms. Goodwin’s home is 70-100 feet from the
  proposed parking lot.

  Lori Barnett, 4 Sunnyfield, stated that she has no problem with the church, however, since
  the school was added there has been an increase in noise and lights that are shining into
  her backyard from Heritage School. Ms. Barnett stated that her property is 10 ft. from the
  parking lot. Also, she stated concerns with a lack of supervision over the middle school
  children and is concerned that the proposed parking will also be used by the school.

  In response to a question by CHAIRMAN YOO, Ms. Barnett stated that she has been
  impacted by the vegetation that was cut down.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Director Wahba stated
  that the building for Peninsula Heritage School was approved in 2015 and there was never
  an intention to have a play area outside of the designated courtyard area adjacent to the
  school.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Director Wahba stated
  that the resolution will address the issue regarding restricting the school in using the
  proposed parking area as a sports court.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed concern for the kids being so far from the school
  and they are not being contained within the permitted area.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Director Wahba stated
  that they are required to receive the water draining downhill. COMMISSIONER SCOTT
  suggested that sand bags be used to protect the parking lot.

  Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, stated that she lives across the street and is not directly
  affected, however, the whole neighborhood is affected by cars going in and out of the
  parking lot. Ms. Wildman stated that she is concerned with long-term planning of the
  property and stated that she does not feel that seven spaces is going to make much of a
  difference. Ms. Wildman suggested finding alternative ways to get people from the parking
  lot to the church entrance, including a lift system. Ms. Wildman stated that she is also
  concerned with losing trees, dirt, and grass throughout the City and pretty soon it will all
  be paved over.

  Gustavo Velasco, 26093 Rolling Hills Road, stated that he has lived at his property since
  2003 and has seen improvements that the church has done. It started as a parking lot for
  the church and a small school. After that, the Montessori school and Heritage Schools
  built structures and it should have been known that there was a need for parking. Mr.
  Velasco stated that he has nothing against the church, however, there is noise and most
  trees were cut down. Mr. Velasco is concerned that this will not only be used as a parking
  lot, but also as a sports court.

  Susan and Luis Guerra, 8 Sunnyfield, stated that their property is behind the proposed
  parking lot. Mr. Guerra stated that there used to be beautiful trees with a nice lawn and
  the property is changing too much. Ms. Guerra stated she is concerned that this project
  is not going to be used for its intended purpose. The parking will still be insufficient and
  the proposed lot is a further walk to the church entrance.

  Dave Sargent, Elder, St. Luke’s Presbyterian Church, stated that by order of the fire
  department, the church spent approximately $13K to fix the situation with overgrown
  vegetation. Mr. Sargent stated that many complaints should be directed to Peninsula
  Heritage Church and stated that the church should be allowed to install a parking lot that
  is level with the church entrance.

  Berdie Wood, Member, St. Luke’s Presbyterian Church, stated that there will be a green
  screen planted and apologized for the piles of rocks.

  Paula Di Fiore, 10 Roanwood Drive, stated that when she has issues with neighbors, she
  speaks to them directly first and stated that she is surprised by the comments from the
  neighbors. Ms. Di Fiore stated that there should be dialogue between the neighbors and
  the church. These are just people trying to do the right thing.

  5
Planning Commission Minutes
September 11, 2017
   Ms. Goodwin stated that the dirt lot was created by the church and stated that the Fire
  Department is not to blame for the issues with the trees.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Pastor Kang stated that the
  church has concerts in June, July, and August and there are no fireworks. Pastor Kang
  added that when they wanted to trim the trees, they were told by tree trimmers that due to
  the Edison power lines, they could not legally trim the trees.

  In a response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Pastor Kang stated that there
  is no official horse trail behind the property and the paddock runs right in line with the
  church property line and water is coming down from an access road and is coming into
  the church property. The sand bags and water is within the property.

  COMMISSIONER SHACHTER MOVED, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER stated that he has a concern that the proposed lot is
  currently being used for parking, which is in violation of the CUP and stated that the
  proposal for seven additional people is not going to resolve the parking issue but will
  impact the neighbors. He stated that a solution could be a shuttle to transport people from
  the parking lot to the church and added that there is a concern that the proposed parking
  lot will be used by the school during the week. He stated that he is opposed to this request
  unless it was restricted to be used only by the church and roped off during the week.

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG stated that the parking lot should be moved closer to the
  sheds and a screening plan needs to be put in place since the trees were cut down. He
  stated that he is opposed to this project as it is presented.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he is sympathetic to what the church is looking for
  but is also sympathetic to the community. He stated that planting hedges are good sound
  diffusers; vegetation issues could be worked out between neighbors. He stated that a
  shuttle bus or lift may not be a feasible solution since it is a small church. The proposed
  parking plan needs to be clear and include a restriction that Peninsula Heritage School
  not use the parking lot, and the use of the school needs to be maintained within the area
  that was approved. The light shining into residences also must be addressed.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that this proposal should come back taking into
  consideration all of the comments and ADA is also important.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that using a shuttle would be less of a burden on
  the neighbors.

  CHAIRMAN YOO stated that seven spaces are not sufficient and there is a lack of trust
  that may not be able to be resolved between the parties. He stated that he is not opposed
  to the parking spaces but there needs to be a comprehensive resolution to noise and
  screening and suggested that the proposal be reworked. CHAIRMAN YOO stated that he
  does not see a shuttle bus to be necessary in this case.

  COMMISSIONER SHACHTER MOVED, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  TO REOPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

  Pastor Kang stated that they would like to bring back a revised proposal taking into
  consideration all concerns. Some alternatives are cost prohibitive.

  CHAIR YOO suggested that there be discussion with the neighbors.

  COMMISSIONER SHACHTER MOVED, SECONDED BY COMMISSIONER SCOTT,

  TO CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING FOR PLANNING APPLICATION 18-17
  TO A DATE UNCERTAIN.

  6
Planning Commission Minutes
September 11, 2017
   Ayes: CHAIR YOO, SCHACHTER, SCOTT, ZIGRANG
  Noes:
  Absent: MEDAWAR, CARMAN
  Abstain:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that this item will be re-noticed two weeks prior to the
  scheduled meeting.

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that hard copies of Municipal Code updates are no
  longer necessary since updates are available on the City website.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  Planning Director Wahba reminded the Planning Commissioners that the City Celebration
  is scheduled on Saturday, September 23, 2017 at Ernie Howlett Park.

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF AUGUST 8, 2017.

  B. DRAFT PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, AUGUST 21,
  2017.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER,

  TO RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11-A AND 11-B.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIRMAN YOO adjourned the meeting at 9:52 p.m.
